question: The Asian Games 2018 were held in which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indonesia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 18th Asian Games (2018) were jointly hosted by Jakarta and Palembang, Indonesia, from 18 August to 2 September 2018. (2018 एशियाई खेल — इंडोनेशिया)

 

• The official slogan of the Games was "Energy of Asia", and the three mascots were Bhin Bhin, Atung and Kaka.

 

• It was the second time Indonesia hosted the Asian Games, the first being in 1962 (Jakarta).

 

• India finished 8th in the medal tally with 70 medals (16 Gold, 23 Silver, 31 Bronze), its best-ever Asian Games performance at the time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2022 Asian Games were originally scheduled for Hangzhou, China, but were postponed to 2023 due to COVID-19.

 

• The next (20th) Asian Games are scheduled for Nagoya, Japan, in 2026.

 

NOTE

 

• South Korea (Option 1): Hosted the Asian Games at Incheon in 2014, not 2018.

 

• Japan (Option 3): Is set to host the Asian Games at Nagoya in 2026.

 

• China (Option 4): Hosted the (postponed) 2022 Asian Games at Hangzhou in 2023, and earlier at Guangzhou (2010) and Beijing (1990).

question: When is Raksha Bandhan celebrated in India as per the Hindu calendar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Poornima, Shravan month.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raksha Bandhan is celebrated on the full moon day (Poornima) of the Hindu lunar month of Shravan (July-August). (रक्षाबंधन — पूर्णिमा, श्रावण मास)

 

• The festival celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters, where the sister ties a sacred thread (rakhi) around her brother's wrist as a symbol of protection.

 

• Shravan Poornima is also observed as Kajari Purnima, Nariyal Purnima (Coconut Day) by fishing communities in coastal Maharashtra/Gujarat, and Rakshabandhan/Upakarma among some Brahmin communities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major festivals tied to Shravan month include Hariyali Teej, Nag Panchami and Shravan Somvar fasts dedicated to Lord Shiva.

 

• Bhai Dooj, another brother-sister festival, is celebrated on the second day after Diwali (Kartik month).

 

NOTE

 

• Amavasya, Shravan month (Option 1) and Amavasya, Ashadha month (Option 3): Raksha Bandhan is observed on Poornima (full moon), not Amavasya (new moon).

 

• Poornima, Ashadha month (Option 2): Incorrect month — Raksha Bandhan falls in Shravan, the month after Ashadha.

question: Protection of life and liberty is included under which Article of the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 21.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 21 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the "Right to Life and Personal Liberty", stating no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. (अनुच्छेद 21 — जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार)

 

• Article 21 falls under Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution, specifically under the head "Right to Freedom".

 

• Through judicial interpretation (e.g., Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, 1978), the Supreme Court has expanded Article 21 to include rights such as the right to privacy, right to a clean environment, right to livelihood, and right to a speedy trial.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21A guarantees the Right to Education for children aged 6-14 years, inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment (2002).

 

• Article 22 provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 23 (Option 2): Prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour (begar).

 

• Article 24 (Option 3): Prohibits employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines or hazardous occupations.

 

• Article 20 (Option 4): Provides protection in respect of conviction for offences (e.g., no ex-post-facto law, no double jeopardy, no self-incrimination).

question: Which of the following is NOT the correct match?
option_1: The acid present in tomato – Formic acid
option_2: The acid present in orange – citric acid
option_3: The acid present in grapes – Tartaric acid
option_4: The acid present in rancid butter – Butyric acid
solution_text:
The correct answer is The acid present in tomato – Formic acid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This is the incorrect match. Tomato mainly contains citric acid and malic acid, not formic acid. (टमाटर का अम्ल — साइट्रिक/मैलिक अम्ल, फॉर्मिक अम्ल नहीं)

 

• Formic acid is actually found in the sting of ants and bees and in the hair of nettle (bichhu buti) leaves — it is not associated with tomato.

 

• The other three matches are chemically correct: orange – citric acid, grapes – tartaric acid, and rancid butter – butyric acid.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vinegar contains acetic acid; curd/yoghurt contains lactic acid; apples contain malic acid; tea contains tannic acid.

 

• Formic acid is also called methanoic acid, the simplest carboxylic acid.

 

NOTE

 

• Orange – citric acid (Option 2): This match is correct — citrus fruits are rich in citric acid.

 

• Grapes – tartaric acid (Option 3): This match is correct — grapes are the primary natural source of tartaric acid.

 

• Rancid butter – butyric acid (Option 4): This match is correct — butyric acid gives rancid butter its characteristic foul odour.

question: The percentage of earth's water found in the oceans is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 97.2 percent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• About 97.2% of the Earth's total water is stored in the oceans and seas as saline water. (पृथ्वी का जल — 97.2% महासागरों में)

 

• Only about 2.8% of Earth's water is fresh water, and most of that (roughly two-thirds) is locked up as ice caps and glaciers.

 

• Less than 1% of all fresh water is easily accessible for human use (rivers, lakes, and groundwater).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• About 71% of the Earth's surface is covered by water, but land area still exceeds habitable freshwater sources significantly.

 

• The largest ocean by area is the Pacific Ocean, followed by the Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic Oceans.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (94%, 90.2%, 92.2%): These figures understate the actual oceanic share; the standard accepted figure is 97.2% (often rounded to 97% or cited as 96.5%).

question: Decadal growth rate of population between 2001-2011 is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 17.70 percent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, India's population grew from 102.87 crore (2001) to 121.09 crore (2011), registering a decadal growth rate of about 17.7% (often cited precisely as 17.64%). (2001-2011 दशकीय वृद्धि दर — 17.7%)

 

• This was a decline from the 2001 Census decadal growth rate of 21.54% (1991-2001), marking a slowdown in India's population growth.

 

• India's 2011 population (121.09 crore) made it the second most populous country in the world after China at that time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2011 Census recorded India's sex ratio as 943 females per 1000 males and literacy rate as 74.04%.

 

• India's 2011 Census was the 15th Census since 1872 and the 7th after Independence.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (18.70%, 15.70%, 16.70%): These do not match the officially recorded 2001-2011 decadal growth rate of 17.7% as per Census of India data.

question: The Paramhans Mandali was founded in 1840 at ___________ to work for the abolition of caste.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Paramhans Mandali was founded in 1840 at Bombay by Dadoba Pandurang, with the aim of abolishing caste restrictions and promoting rational, monotheistic worship. (परमहंस मंडली — बॉम्बे, 1840)

 

• Members of the Mandali secretly defied caste rules — for instance, dining together across castes — though it functioned largely as a secret society and eventually declined by the 1860s.

 

• It is considered one of the earliest socio-religious reform organisations in western India, predating the Prarthana Samaj (1867).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Prarthana Samaj, founded in 1867 in Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang (with later leadership from M.G. Ranade), carried forward similar reformist ideas.

 

• The Brahmo Samaj (Calcutta, 1828, by Raja Ram Mohan Roy) was another major contemporary reform movement working against social evils, though focused more in Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Delhi (Option 1), Calcutta (Option 2) and Madras (Option 4): The Paramhans Mandali was specifically a Bombay-based organisation and was not founded in these cities.

question: Who was the Mughal emperor, when a massive rebellion against british rule broke out in 1857?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bahadur Shah Zafar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bahadur Shah Zafar II was the last Mughal emperor, reigning from 1837 to 1857, and was the nominal/symbolic leader of the Revolt of 1857. (1857 का विद्रोह — बहादुर शाह जफर)

 

• The revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857 and rebel sepoys marched to Delhi, proclaiming Bahadur Shah Zafar as the Emperor of India.

 

• After the revolt was suppressed, the British exiled him to Rangoon (Burma), where he died in 1862, marking the formal end of the Mughal dynasty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Following the 1857 revolt, the Government of India Act, 1858 transferred control of India from the East India Company to the British Crown.

 

• Bahadur Shah Zafar was also a noted Urdu poet, writing under the pen name "Zafar".

 

NOTE

 

• Farrukhsiyar (Option 1): A Mughal emperor of the early 18th century (1713-1719), known for granting the East India Company duty-free trade rights via a farman in 1717.

 

• Akbar II (Option 3): Reigned from 1806 to 1837; he was the father of Bahadur Shah Zafar, and preceded him, not present in 1857.

 

• Aurangzeb (Option 4): The last major Mughal emperor of the empire's peak, ruling 1658-1707, long before 1857.

question: The motion of ______ body is an example of uniformly accelerated motion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is freely falling.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A freely falling body (falling under gravity alone, with no air resistance) is the classic textbook example of uniformly accelerated motion, since it experiences a constant acceleration equal to ‘g’ (~9.8 m/s²). (मुक्त रूप से गिरता पिंड — एकसमान त्वरित गति)

 

• Uniformly accelerated motion means the velocity changes by an equal amount in equal intervals of time, i.e., acceleration remains constant in magnitude and direction.

 

• The equations of motion (v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as) are directly applicable to a freely falling body by substituting a = g.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A body moving in a straight line with constant speed has zero acceleration (uniform, not accelerated, motion).

 

• Circular motion at constant speed involves centripetal acceleration, but its direction constantly changes, so it is not ‘uniformly accelerated’ in the simple linear sense.

 

NOTE

 

• Resting body (Option 1): A body at rest has zero velocity and zero acceleration — it is not accelerating at all.

 

• Decelerating body (Option 2): Decreasing speed implies acceleration opposite to velocity; this is only uniformly accelerated if the deceleration itself is constant, but this is not the standard textbook example.

 

• Parabolic motion (Option 3): This describes projectile motion (a combination of uniform horizontal velocity and vertically accelerated motion) — it is not itself the standard example of purely uniform acceleration.

question: Gross primary deficit is the difference between ______.
option_2: gross fiscal deficit and interest receipts
option_4: gross fiscal deficit and net interest liabilities
solution_text:
The correct answer is gross fiscal deficit and net interest liabilities.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gross Primary Deficit is defined as Gross Fiscal Deficit minus Net Interest Liabilities (interest payments minus interest receipts) of the government. (सकल प्राथमिक घाटा — सकल राजकोषीय घाटा − शुद्ध ब्याज देयताएँ)

 

• It reflects the government's borrowing requirement excluding interest payments, i.e., how much the government needs to borrow for expenses other than servicing past debt.

 

• A zero primary deficit means the government does not need to borrow beyond what is required to pay interest on its existing debt.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts (excluding borrowings).

 

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts, indicating dissaving on the government's revenue account.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1 and 3 (involving revenue deficit): Primary deficit is derived from the fiscal deficit, not the revenue deficit.

 

• Option 2 (gross fiscal deficit and interest receipts): Incorrect — the correct subtrahend is net interest liabilities (net of both interest payments and receipts), not interest receipts alone.

question: Which of the following folk dances does NOT belong to the state of Madhya Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Laho.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Laho is a folk dance of Meghalaya, performed by the Jaintia (Pnar) tribe, generally around harvest festivals — it does not belong to Madhya Pradesh. (लाहो नृत्य — मेघालय, मध्य प्रदेश का नहीं)

 

• Matki, Jawara, and Phulpati are all well-known folk dances of Madhya Pradesh, often performed during harvest and festival seasons by various tribal and rural communities of the state.

 

• Madhya Pradesh's major folk/tribal dances also include Grida, Saila, Karma, Baredi, and Bhagoria.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Karma dance, performed to worship the Karam tree/deity, is common to Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Jharkhand tribal belts.

 

• Bhagoria is a colourful festival-dance of the Bhil and Bhilala tribes of western Madhya Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Phulpati (Option 2): A folk dance of Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Matki (Option 3): A folk dance of the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh, performed by women balancing pots (matki) on their heads.

 

• Jawara (Option 4): A folk dance of Madhya Pradesh, performed during the Jawara festival linked to the harvest of the jowar/wheat crop.

question: Which of the following venues was decided to host the 2022 Asian Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hangzhou, China.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hangzhou, China, was selected to host the 19th Asian Games (2022). (2022 एशियाई खेल — हांगझोऊ, चीन)

 

• The Games were originally scheduled for 10-25 September 2022, but were postponed to 23 September - 8 October 2023 due to the COVID-19 pandemic in China, while retaining the official name "2022 Asian Games".

 

• The official mascots were three robots — Congcong, Lianlian, and Chenchen — and the slogan was "Heart to Heart, @Future".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• China topped the medal tally at the 2022/2023 Asian Games, followed by Japan and South Korea; India finished 4th with a record 107 medals.

 

• The next (20th) Asian Games are scheduled to be held in Nagoya, Japan, in 2026.

 

NOTE

 

• Guangzhou, China (Option 2): Hosted the 2010 Asian Games, not 2022.

 

• Incheon, South Korea (Option 3): Hosted the 2014 Asian Games.

 

• Jakarta, Indonesia (Option 4): Co-hosted (with Palembang) the 2018 Asian Games.

question: The Revolutionary Socialist Party was established in ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1940.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Revolutionary Socialist Party (RSP) was formed on 19 March 1940, evolving from remnants of the revolutionary nationalist Anushilan Samiti movement in Bengal. (क्रांतिकारी समाजवादी पार्टी — 1940)

 

• It emerged with a Marxist-Leninist ideological orientation, moving from armed revolutionary nationalism towards organised socialist politics.

 

• The RSP is a recognised political party in India, historically strong in West Bengal, Kerala, and Tripura.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Anushilan Samiti, from which many RSP founders emerged, was originally established in 1902 in Calcutta.

 

• Other socialist-origin parties in India include the Communist Party of India (CPI, 1925) and the Congress Socialist Party (CSP, 1934).

 

NOTE

 

• 1936, 1925 and 1929 (Options 1, 2 and 4): These years do not correspond to the RSP's founding; 1925 is instead associated with the founding of the Communist Party of India at Kanpur.

question: Singers Sujatha and Ananthu have been awarded the Kalaimamani Award for the year ____________ by the Tamil Nadu Government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2021.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Playback singers Sujatha Mohan and Ananthu were conferred the Kalaimamani Award for the year 2021 by the Government of Tamil Nadu. (कलैमामणि पुरस्कार — तमिलनाडु सरकार)

 

• The Kalaimamani Award is the highest civilian honour of the Tamil Nadu government, presented annually by the Tamil Nadu Eyal Isai Nataka Manram (Iyal Isai Nataka Mandram) for outstanding contributions to art, literature, and culture.

 

• Sujatha Mohan is a well-known Indian playback singer noted for her work in Tamil, Malayalam, and other South Indian film industries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kalaimamani award covers diverse fields including music, dance, drama, cinema, and literature.

 

• Recent notable Kalaimamani awardees include actors and artists honoured periodically by the Tamil Nadu government across various years.

 

NOTE

 

• 2022, 2019 and 2020 (Options 1, 2 and 4): These years are incorrect — Sujatha and Ananthu received the honour specifically for the year 2021.

question: Which of the following element is more reactive than copper?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zinc.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the reactivity series of metals, Zinc (Zn) stands above Copper (Cu), making it more reactive. (धातु क्रियाशीलता श्रेणी — जिंक, कॉपर से अधिक क्रियाशील)

 

• The standard reactivity series (most to least reactive) is roughly: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > (H) > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au > Pt.

 

• Because zinc is more reactive than copper, it can displace copper from copper sulphate solution: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu, a classic displacement reaction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gold, Silver, and Platinum are classified as noble metals because of their low reactivity and resistance to corrosion/oxidation.

 

• Zinc is used to galvanise iron (zinc coating) precisely because it is more reactive and corrodes preferentially, protecting the iron underneath.

 

NOTE

 

• Gold (Option 1): Placed below copper in the reactivity series — far less reactive.

 

• Silver (Option 3): Also placed below copper, being a noble/less reactive metal.

 

• Platinum (Option 4): One of the least reactive metals, placed at the very bottom of the reactivity series.

question: The New Delhi International Arbitration Centre (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was introduced in Lok Sabha on _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is August 5, 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The New Delhi International Arbitration Centre (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 5 August 2022. (नई दिल्ली अंतरराष्ट्रीय मध्यस्थता केंद्र संशोधन विधेयक — 5 अगस्त 2022)

 

• The Bill amended the New Delhi International Arbitration Centre Act, 2019, and notably renamed the institution from ‘New Delhi International Arbitration Centre (NDIAC)’ to the ‘India International Arbitration Centre (IIAC)’.

 

• The Bill was aimed at making the arbitration centre a flagship institution for conducting international and domestic arbitration and improving India's ease of doing business/dispute resolution ecosystem.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The original NDIAC Act, 2019 replaced the International Centre for Alternative Dispute Resolution (ICADR), taking over its undertakings.

 

• The renamed India International Arbitration Centre (IIAC) formally came into force in January 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• June 8, 2022 (Option 1), October 7, 2022 (Option 2) and September 6, 2022 (Option 3): These dates do not correspond to the Bill's introduction — it was introduced in Lok Sabha specifically on 5 August 2022.

question: Who has been named as the next chairperson of the Securities and Exchange Board of India in March 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhabi Puri Buch.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Madhabi Puri Buch was named in March 2022 as the next Chairperson of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), taking charge on 1 March 2022. (सेबी अध्यक्ष — माधबी पुरी बुच)

 

• She became the first woman to head SEBI and also the first person from the private sector to be appointed as SEBI Chairperson.

 

• She succeeded Ajay Tyagi as SEBI Chairperson.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• SEBI was established in 1988 and given statutory powers under the SEBI Act, 1992; it is headquartered in Mumbai.

 

• SEBI regulates India's securities and capital markets, protecting investor interests and promoting market development.

 

NOTE

 

• Debasish Panda (Option 1): Served as Chairperson of IRDAI (insurance regulator), not SEBI.

 

• T. Raja Kumar (Option 3): Served as President of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), an international body, not SEBI.

 

• Ashwani Bhatia (Option 4): Has served as a Whole Time Member of SEBI, not as its Chairperson.

question: Mangubhai Chhaganbhai Patel was appointed as the Governor of ____________ in July 2021.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mangubhai Chhaganbhai Patel was appointed as the Governor of Madhya Pradesh in July 2021. (मंगूभाई छगनभाई पटेल — मध्य प्रदेश के राज्यपाल)

 

• He took the oath of office on 8 July 2021, succeeding Anandiben Patel, who was transferred to Uttar Pradesh.

 

• Prior to this, he had earlier served as the Governor of Goa.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Governors of Indian states are appointed by the President of India under Article 155 of the Constitution, usually for a 5-year term, serving at the President's pleasure.

 

• Anandiben Patel moved from Madhya Pradesh to become Governor of Uttar Pradesh around the same reshuffle in July 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 2): Had Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar as Governor around this period (later Governors have also served since).

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Anandiben Patel was appointed Governor of Uttar Pradesh in July 2021, not Mangubhai Patel.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 4): Had a different Governor (e.g., B.D. Mishra) during this period, not Mangubhai Patel.

question: How much purse money was given to a Sangeet Natak Akademi fellow in 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ₹3 lakh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna), the highest honour conferred by the Akademi, carries a purse money of ₹3 lakh, along with a Tamrapatra (copper plaque) and an Angavastram. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी फेलोशिप — 3 लाख रुपये)

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, established in 1952, is India's national academy for music, dance, and drama, and is the first National Academy of Arts set up by independent India.

 

• The regular Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) carries a comparatively lower purse money along with a plaque and angavastram.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi is headquartered in New Delhi and functions under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.

 

• Fellows are referred to as "Akademi Ratna" (formerly "Akademi Fellows"), a title of highest distinction in the performing arts.

 

NOTE

 

• ₹4 lakh, ₹2 lakh and ₹1 lakh (Options 1, 3 and 4): These figures do not match the officially notified purse money for the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship, which is ₹3 lakh.

question: Which of the following animals have a single opening in their digestive system that serves both as a mouth and an anus?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Platyhelminthes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Platyhelminthes (flatworms), such as Planaria and tapeworms, possess an incomplete digestive system with a single opening that functions as both the mouth and the anus. (चपटे कृमि — एक ही द्वार, मुख और गुदा दोनों)

 

• This is a characteristic feature of simpler, more primitively organised bilaterian animals, in contrast to organisms with a complete (through-gut) digestive system having separate mouth and anus.

 

• Other phyla sharing this trait of a single digestive opening include Cnidaria (e.g., Hydra, jellyfish) and Ctenophora.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Animals with a complete alimentary canal (separate mouth and anus) include Annelids, Arthropods, Molluscs, Echinoderms, and Chordates, allowing more efficient, one-directional digestion.

 

• Platyhelminthes are acoelomate (lacking a true body cavity) and are classified as triploblastic animals.

 

NOTE

 

• Arachnids (Option 1): Members of Phylum Arthropoda; they possess a complete digestive system with separate mouth and anus.

 

• Echinoderms (Option 2): (e.g., starfish, sea urchins) have a complete digestive system with distinct mouth and anus (with some larval exceptions).

 

• Arthropods (Option 4): Possess a well-developed, complete digestive tract with separate mouth and anus.

question: Which of the following city of India was a coastal settlement where ships unloaded goods from distant lands between 2200 and 1900 years ago?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arikamedu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arikamedu, located near Puducherry on the Coromandel Coast, was an important ancient coastal trading settlement where ships from distant lands (including the Roman/Mediterranean world) unloaded goods roughly 2200 to 1900 years ago. (अरिकामेडु — प्राचीन तटीय व्यापारिक बंदरगाह)

 

• Archaeological excavations at Arikamedu (notably by Mortimer Wheeler in 1945) uncovered Roman amphorae, Arretine ware pottery, beads, and other artefacts, confirming Indo-Roman trade contacts.

 

• The site indicates a flourishing trade in items such as spices, textiles, gems, and glassware, exchanged with the Mediterranean/Roman world via maritime routes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important ancient Indian ports engaged in maritime trade include Muziris (Kerala coast) and Barygaza/Bharuch (Gujarat coast) on the western seaboard.

 

• Evidence of Indo-Roman trade also includes Roman coin hoards found at various sites across peninsular India.

 

NOTE

 

• Karaikal (Option 1), Veerampattinam (Option 2) and Yanam (Option 3): These are coastal towns of the Puducherry Union Territory/nearby Coromandel coast, but the site specifically identified with 2200-1900-year-old maritime trade archaeology is Arikamedu.

question: Which of the following is soda lime?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NaOH + CaO.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Soda lime is a mixture of Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH) and Calcium Oxide (CaO), prepared by slaking quicklime with concentrated sodium hydroxide solution. (सोडा लाइम — NaOH + CaO)

 

• It is a white, solid, alkaline mixture used to absorb carbon dioxide and moisture in laboratories, and also used in carbon dioxide scrubbers (e.g., in anaesthesia machines, submarines, and rebreathers).

 

• Soda lime is also used in the laboratory preparation of methane, by heating sodium acetate with soda lime (CH₃COONa + NaOH → CH₄ + Na₂CO₃, with CaO acting as a diluent to control the reaction).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Quicklime refers to CaO (calcium oxide) alone, while slaked lime refers to Ca(OH)₂ (calcium hydroxide).

 

• Soda lime is distinct from washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) and baking soda (NaHCO₃), which are different sodium compounds.

 

NOTE

 

• Ca(OH)₂ + CaO (Option 1): This combination does not define soda lime; Ca(OH)₂ is slaked lime on its own.

 

• KOH + CaO (Option 2): Uses potassium hydroxide instead of sodium hydroxide — not the standard composition of soda lime.

 

• CaCl₂ + CaO (Option 3): Calcium chloride mixed with calcium oxide does not constitute soda lime; CaCl₂ is itself commonly used as a separate drying agent.

question: The Centre introduced a new bill called the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill 2022. This Bill will repeal the Identification of Prisoners Act which was established in _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1920.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill, 2022 (later the Act, 2022) repealed the colonial-era Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920. (पहचान अधिनियम — 1920 का कानून निरस्त)

 

• The new law expands the categories of data (measurements) that can be collected from convicts and certain other persons — including biometric, fingerprint, iris, retina scans, and physical/biological samples — for use in criminal investigation.

 

• The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 28 March 2022 by the Ministry of Home Affairs and was subsequently passed by Parliament in April 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under the new Act, collected data can be retained for up to 75 years by the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), which is authorised to store and manage such records.

 

• The original 1920 Act allowed only the taking of fingerprints and footprints of a limited category of convicted persons, which the 2022 Act substantially broadened.

 

NOTE

 

• 1930, 1950 and 1945 (Options 1, 2 and 3): None of these years correspond to the enactment of the Identification of Prisoners Act, which was passed specifically in 1920.

question: Where was the first Jute factory in India established?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rishra, West Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first jute mill/factory in India was established at Rishra, near Kolkata, West Bengal, in 1855 by George Acland. (प्रथम जूट मिल — रिशरा, पश्चिम बंगाल, 1855)

 

• This marked the beginning of mechanised jute manufacturing in India, and the region along the Hooghly River subsequently became a major hub of the jute industry.

 

• By the late 19th and early 20th centuries, Bengal (particularly around Kolkata) had become the world's leading centre for jute processing and export, earning India the title of the world's largest jute producer and exporter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India remains the world's largest producer of jute, with West Bengal contributing the majority share of production.

 

• Jute is often referred to as the "Golden Fibre" of India due to its economic importance and golden-brown colour.

 

NOTE

 

• Cuttack, Odisha (Option 1), Ongole, Andhra Pradesh (Option 2) and Raigarh, Chhattisgarh (Option 4): None of these locations hosted India's first jute factory; the historically correct site is Rishra, West Bengal.

question: In which of the following states was ‘Kudumbashree,’ women-oriented, community–based, poverty-reduction programme implemented?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ‘Kudumbashree’ is a women-oriented, community-based, poverty-reduction programme launched by the Government of Kerala in 1998. (कुदुम्बश्री — केरल की महिला-केंद्रित गरीबी उन्मूलन योजना)

 

• It operates through a three-tier Community Development Society (CDS) structure — Neighbourhood Groups (NHGs) at the base, Area Development Societies (ADS) at the ward level, and Community Development Societies (CDS) at the local body level.

 

• Kudumbashree is implemented in partnership with the State Poverty Eradication Mission (SPEM) of Kerala and focuses on micro-credit, entrepreneurship, and empowerment of women for poverty alleviation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kudumbashree is often cited as one of the largest women's empowerment/self-help group networks in the world, covering millions of women members across Kerala.

 

• Kerala's Kudumbashree model has been studied and partially replicated as a reference for poverty-reduction and self-help group (SHG) programmes in other states.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh (Options 1, 3 and 4): These states run their own distinct poverty-alleviation/SHG programmes (e.g., Bihar's JEEViKA), but ‘Kudumbashree’ specifically is a Kerala initiative.
